````text
# #2844: Patch: the stats drill-down's loading skeleton fills its column on a phone
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

## What happens

On a phone (jackioh.vercel.app, iOS, about 390px wide), opening a card's drill-down on **/stats** (seen with Traitorous Blood) shows the loading skeleton under the Show Radiant / View in Almanac buttons squeezed into a strip about 80px wide. What's left is the row skeleton's 28px round marks, two of them visible, and a sliver of the JackiOh mark cut off on both sides. None of the skeleton's lines show.

## Why

`apps/web/src/routes/stats.css`, the `@media (max-width: 640px)` rule, sets `.stats-drilldown-body { flex-direction: column; align-items: center; }`. In a column, `align-items: center` shrinks `.stats-drilldown-details` to its content's width. The `Skeleton` (`apps/web/src/skeleton/`, `variant="rows"`, "Loading this card's details…") is `width: 100%` of that shrunk column, so each row's `.skeleton__line` (`flex: 1 1 auto`) gets no width. The `.skeleton__blocks::before` mark also gets clipped by the root's `overflow: hidden`.

The loaded details probably sit in the same shrink-wrapped column too. Their text sizes the column, so the problem is less visible there.

## What should happen

At phone width, the details column under the card is as wide as the dialog's body. The skeleton then draws full-width rows with the mark centered and whole, as it does on desktop beside the card. The card preview, the actions and the tokens stay centered as now.

## Suggested fix

Inside the `max-width: 640px` block, give `.stats-drilldown-details` `align-self: stretch` (or `width: 100%`). Leave the desktop row layout alone. Its `align-items: flex-start` is pinned by the existing test.

## Test

jsdom lays nothing out, so do what the existing `describe("the drill-down's card preview")` test in `apps/web/src/routes/stats.test.tsx` does: read `stats.css` and assert that the phone media block stretches `.stats-drilldown-details`. Add it beside that test.

## Where

- `apps/web/src/routes/stats.css` (the drill-down's mobile rule, near `/* Mobile responsive */`)
- `apps/web/src/routes/stats.test.tsx`

Client CSS only. No engine, card or catalog change, and no ruling needed.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-8` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41490489288)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

On a phone (`max-width: 640px`), the /stats drill-down's details column, `.stats-drilldown-details`, which holds the loading `Skeleton` (`variant="rows"`, "Loading this card's details…") and then the loaded details, stretches to the full width of `.stats-drilldown-body`. It no longer shrinks to its content's width. The skeleton then draws full-width rows with its mark whole. The card preview, the actions and the tokens stay centered, and the desktop row layout (`align-items: flex-start`) is unchanged. A unit test reads `stats.css` and proves that the phone block stretches the details column.

## Files to touch

| File | new/change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/routes/stats.css` | change | Inside the `/* Mobile responsive */` `@media (max-width: 640px)` block: a new `.stats-drilldown-details { align-self: stretch; }` rule with a short comment |
| `apps/web/src/routes/stats.test.tsx` | change | One new `it` in `describe("the drill-down's card preview")`, right after the first `it` |

Do not touch anything else. That means `apps/web/src/routes/stats.tsx`, `apps/web/src/skeleton/` (`Skeleton.tsx`, `skeleton.css`), any other CSS, `spec/`, `crates/`, `e2e/`, and every `package.json` and config. This is client CSS only. No spec section or ruling governs it, and no R number is added or cited. CLAUDE.md rule 7 holds: nothing here touches what the client knows.

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/routes/stats.css`, the phone block (now lines 704–710).** Leave the existing `.stats-drilldown-body` rule inside the block as it is. After it, inside the same `@media`, add one blank line and then this rule, so that the block reads exactly:

   ```css
   /* Mobile responsive */
   @media (max-width: 640px) {
     .stats-drilldown-body {
       flex-direction: column;
       align-items: center;
     }

     /* Stretched, not centered: centered, the column shrank to its content and the loading skeleton's
        rows (`width: 100%` of it) had no room left for their lines. */
     .stats-drilldown-details {
       align-self: stretch;
     }
   }
   ```

   Do not change the desktop `.stats-drilldown-body` rule (line 562, `align-items: flex-start`) or the desktop `.stats-drilldown-details` rule (line 667). Do not add `width: 100%`. Keep the media block's closing `}` at column 0 on its own line: the test's regex depends on it.

2. **`apps/web/src/routes/stats.test.tsx`, `describe("the drill-down's card preview")` (line 1262).** Right after the closing `});` of its first test, `it("keeps the face at 5:7 however long the details column runs", …)` (ends at line 1271), and before `it("shows the Radiant face beside the normal one …")`, add a blank line and then this test. It reuses the file's existing `readFileSync`, `resolve` and `HERE` imports and needs no new import:

   ```ts
   it("stretches the details column to the body's width on a phone, so the loading skeleton draws its rows", () => {
     // In the phone's column the body centers its items, which shrank the details column to its
     // content and left the skeleton's rows (`width: 100%` of it) no room for their lines.
     const css = readFileSync(resolve(HERE, "stats.css"), "utf8").replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, "");
     const phone = /@media\s*\(max-width:\s*640px\)\s*\{([\s\S]*?)\n\}/.exec(css)?.[1] ?? "";
     const body = /\.stats-drilldown-body\s*\{([^}]*)\}/.exec(phone)?.[1] ?? "";
     expect(body).toMatch(/flex-direction:\s*column/);
     expect(body).toMatch(/align-items:\s*center/);
     const details = /\.stats-drilldown-details\s*\{([^}]*)\}/.exec(phone)?.[1] ?? "";
     expect(details).toMatch(/align-self:\s*stretch/);
   });
   ```

   Indent it two spaces, like the tests beside it. Do not edit the first test: its regex still matches the desktop `.stats-drilldown-body` rule, the first one in the file.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/routes/stats.test.tsx`, the new `it("stretches the details column to the body's width on a phone, so the loading skeleton draws its rows")`. It asserts three things about the `@media (max-width: 640px)` block of `stats.css`, with comments stripped: its `.stats-drilldown-body` keeps `flex-direction: column` and `align-items: center` (the preview, actions and tokens stay centered), and its `.stats-drilldown-details` has `align-self: stretch`. Without step 1 the `details` match is `""` and the last `expect` fails. The planner checked the same regexes with node against the current `stats.css` (fails) and a copy with step 1 applied (passes, and the existing desktop `flex-start` test still passes).
- The existing `it("keeps the face at 5:7 however long the details column runs")` must still pass unchanged.

Commands, from the repository root. The WebAssembly package is not built in a fresh worktree, so build it first:

```
sh scripts/build-wasm.sh
pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/routes/stats.test.tsx
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck
pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/routes/stats.test.tsx
```

## Done when

- [ ] In `stats.css`, the `max-width: 640px` block holds `.stats-drilldown-details { align-self: stretch; }`, and its `.stats-drilldown-body` rule is unchanged.
- [ ] The desktop `.stats-drilldown-body` (`align-items: flex-start`) and `.stats-drilldown-details` rules are unchanged.
- [ ] The new test and every other test in `src/routes/stats.test.tsx` pass.
- [ ] The web typecheck and eslint are clean for the touched test file.
- [ ] The harness's checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests and web tests. None of them reads these files except the web tests.
- [ ] `git status` shows only the two files in the table changed.

## Risks

- **The desktop layout.** The new rule sits only inside the phone `@media`, so the side-by-side layout and the pinned `align-items: flex-start` are untouched.
- **The test's media regex.** It ends the block at the first `\n}`. Inner rules close with an indented `  }`, so the block's own `}` must stay at column 0. A reformat that breaks this makes the test fail rather than pass falsely.
- **The loaded details.** They sit in the same column and become full width on a phone. This is what the issue asks for ("as wide as the dialog's body").
- No engine, replay, hidden-information or wire change. `apps/web/src/wire/` is not touched.

## Open questions

- Decision the issue left open: `align-self: stretch` rather than `width: 100%`. Stretch overrides only this item's centering. `width: 100%` would do the same here (the column has no padding), but it is a second way to say it, and the issue lists stretch first.
- The planner could not see GitHub, so it could not check that no open pull request touches `stats.css` or `stats.test.tsx` (easy rule, line 9).
````
